facts.text: Sensor calibration measures a sensor's internal intrinsic properties and its external position and angle on a machine so that readings can be placed correctly in the real world.
facts.quote: Calibration is the measurement of how a sensor sees (its internal, intrinsic properties) and where it sits on the machine (its external, extrinsic position and angle), so that its readings can be placed correctly in the real world.

facts.text: Sensor calibration should be logged per run with drift checks, mounting revision and frame conventions because calibration is part of the data.
facts.quote: Calibration is part of the data, not background. It should be logged per run with drift checks, mounting revision and frame conventions

facts.text: Without sensor coordinate transforms, sensor readings cannot later be projected into a common frame.

facts.text: Vibration on rough terrain is documented to shift sensor calibration.

facts.text: Several accurate sensors can build an inaccurate scene if their coordinate transforms or timestamps are wrong.
